newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNI FOCUS - prices flat, searching for supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNI FOCUS - prices flat, searching for supply.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices were talked from flat to down about an eighth of a point in early afternoon trade on Thursday as the market wound down ahead of the three-day U.S. Memorial Day weekend.
Traders said that the firmness seen in the June municipal bond futures, which widened the gap between these contracts and June Treasury bond futures, largely reflected the lack of supply.
"The MOB is screaming because people can't replace anything," a trader said.
Another trader added that the firmness displayed by the June municipal bond futures was not seen in the cash marekt.

While a couple of large bid-wanted lists were being circulated, traders said that when the bonds being advertized for sale were added up, along with a few smaller lists, they only totaled from around $180 million to $200 million, a level considered moderate.
Issues with the magic yield of six percent or higher, which is seen as magnet for retail demand, were in short supply.
"Anything above six percent, you can't even find it. A lot of the mature, health-care deals are starting to dry up," a trader said.

While health-care bonds often sell at higher yields, due to the risks that the issuer might have to cope with big cutbacks in programs like Medicaid, which helps pay for healthcare for the needy, and Medicare, which helps cover costs for retirees, the trader noted that spreads for this type of paper were narrowing. "It used to be a 10-basis point spread off insured AA, now it's down to like a five."

June municipal bond futures gained four ticks to 116-10/32, while June Treasury bond futures fell six ticks to 109-3/32. This left the MOB spread at a strong 231 ticks, continuing its recent drive higher.
In the secondary market, Alliance Airport Authority Inc, Texas, Special Facilities Revenues of 2021, which pay a 6-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 101-1/4, up an eighth of a point.
And Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.68 percent, NET, up two basis points.
